title: Subject Pronouns
summary: Learn the Brazilian Portuguese subject pronouns (eu, você, ele/ela...) and how 'você' replaces 'tu' in most of Brazil.

sections.heading: The pronouns
sections.body:
Portuguese subject pronouns tell us **who** performs the action. In Brazilian Portuguese, the everyday set is:

| Person | Pronoun | English |
|---|---|---|
| 1st sing. | **eu** | I |
| 2nd sing. | **você** | you |
| 3rd sing. | **ele / ela** | he / she |
| 1st plur. | **nós** (or *a gente*) | we |
| 2nd plur. | **vocês** | you (all) |
| 3rd plur. | **eles / elas** | they |

sections.heading: 'Você' instead of 'tu'
sections.body: European Portuguese uses **tu** for informal 'you', but most of Brazil uses **você** for both formal and informal situations. **Você** takes *third-person* verb forms (the same as *ele/ela*), which makes conjugation easier for beginners.

examples.note: 'você é' uses the same verb form as 'ele é'.
'a gente' means 'we' but takes singular verbs — extremely common in speech.
vocês = plural you and uses são.

sections.heading: Dropping the pronoun
sections.body: Because the verb ending often shows the person, Brazilians frequently **omit** the subject pronoun when it is clear from context.

examples.note: 'Eu' is dropped — the form 'sou' already means 'I am'.
Eles/elas can be dropped when context is clear.

keyPoints: 'A gente' is a very common colloquial way to say 'we' and takes singular verbs.
Subject pronouns are often dropped when the verb ending makes the subject clear.

commonMistakes.note: In most of Brazil, use 'você' + 3rd-person verb, not 'tu és'.
'A gente' takes a singular verb even though it means 'we'.
Você is singular; vocês is plural.
